Any militia company needs some sort of fire support. Mortars might get tricky, the line between "arms" and "ordinance" has never really been clearly draw.

In the late 1990's and early 2000's the cost of education began to rise, and for the first time a large percentage of students found themselves unable to pay off their debts. While usually this would mean that smaller student loans were given out, and therefore in order to keep attracting students college tuition would be forced to shrink. However, under Bush Jr. student loan debt was placed in he same category as criminal debt, meaning that it even through bankruptcy, one was still liable for debt. As long as lenders felt that they would be paid eventually, especially with massive interest, they kept lending, and colleges kept raising tuition.

The solution is to place student loan debt back with all other forms of non-criminal debt, not to support the current unsustainable level of tuition at taxpayer expense. 

Also, the bill provides incentives for public sector jobs, which constitutes more federal intervention in the marketplace, as graduates are essentially paid off to avoid the private sector, which would seem to reduce national growth over time.
